questions.question: The natural aging of a lake by nutrient enrichment of its water is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**eutrophication**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a body of water becomes **highly mineralized and nutrient-rich, **planktonic algae develop rapidly as a result of this.
 
• **Eutrophication** is the process of excessive growth of planktonic algae in nutrient-rich water.
 
• Hypoxia is formed as a result of excessive planktonic algae development, which leads to the death of aquatic animals due to low oxygen levels and the gradual disappearance of the lake.
 
• **Excess phosphorus** is usually always the source of eutrophication in freshwater ecosystems, but nitrogen and phosphorus may play diverse roles in marine habitats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plankton** is a varied group of organisms that live in water and are unable to swim against the stream. 
 
• **Biomagnification** is the accumulation of a chemical by an organism as a result of water and food exposure, resulting in a concentration that is higher than would have been expected from equilibrium if the chemical had only been exposed to water.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the organisation of village panchayats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 40**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **One of the Directive Principles of State Policy enshrined in Article 40** of the Indian Constitution is that the State shall take all necessary steps to **organise local panchayats.**
 
• The state shall grant village panchayats such rights and authority as may be required to allow them to act as self-governing bodies.
 
• The key characteristics of Panchayati Raj Institutions must provide them with certainty, consistency, and strength.
 
• For the benefit of society and rural areas, the relevant state government must effectively **manage the system and organise village governments**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 39 **of the Indian Constitution deals directly with the laws or policy concepts that the government must follow. Article 39 has six sub-clauses, including, All citizens, regardless of their sex, whether men or women, should have an equal right to appropriate means of subsistence.
 
• **Article 38** of the Indian Constitution mandates that the state shall maintain a social order that promotes people's welfare.
 
• "The provisions included in this Part (Part IV) shall not be enforceable by any court,"** according to Article 37**, "but the concepts given down therein are nonetheless vital in the government of the country, and it shall be the obligation of the State to apply these principles in drafting laws."

questions.question: Which of the following is an initiative aimed at preventing hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks, and promote their mechanised cleaning?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Safaimitra Suraksha Challenge-2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **On November 19, 2020, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) **launched the** Safaimitra Suraksha Challenge-2021** in honour of **World Toilet Day**.
 
• Its goal is to increase mechanised cleaning of sewers and septic tanks while avoiding harmful cleaning.
 
• It also wants to focus on the following aspects: mechanical sewage and septic tank cleaning to reduce the need for human entrance, providing suitable protective wear and equipment, and identifying and integrating informal labour into formal mechanisms.
 
• **246 cities **were nominated to take part in this initiative. During the Safaimitra Suraksha Challenge, field inspections were conducted in these cities, with a total of** 31000+ feedback received**.
 
• Call centres and helpline numbers for safe cleaning have been established in 345 cities as part of the Safaimitra Suraksha Challenge (SSC), with the '14420' helpline number being used to date for safe cleaning of septic tanks/sewers and submitting complaints on hazardous cleaning.
 
• The Responsible Sanitation Authority (RSA) has been established in 31 states/UTs, and the Sanitation Response Units have been established in 210 cities (SRU).

questions.question: Kathak exponent and Padma Vibhushan awardee Pt Birju Maharaj was the torchbearer of which gharana of the Lucknow style of Kathak?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalka-Bindadin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj **was an Indian Kathak dancer, composer, singer, and exponent of the** Banaras Gharana's "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana**.
 
• His two uncles, Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj, as well as his father and guru, Acchan Maharaj, were all Kathak dancers.
 
• He was also a vocalist who sang Hindustani classical music. After working at Bhartiya Kala Kendra, then the Kathak Kendra, New Delhi, with his uncle Shambhu Maharaj, he became the head of the latter for several years until his retirement in 1998, when he started his own dance school, **Kalashram**, also in Delhi.
 
• In 1986, Birju Maharaj received the** Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian honour. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Raigarh** is renowned as the 'Cultural Capital of Chhattisgarh,' and is known for its classical music and the dance genre "Kathak" (as Raigarh Gharana).
 
• **Bhanu Ji Maharaj **founded the **Kathak Gharana of Jaipur**. He learned Shiv Tandav from a saint and proceeded to teach it to future generations. Shiv Tandav is a Kathak dance genre that is forceful.
 
• Renowned Kathak dancer Janakiprasad created the Kathak** Banaras Gharana**.

questions.question: Which of the following terms, also known as hypersensitivity, is used to describe a condition in which the human body has an exaggerated response to a substance (e.g. food or drug)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allergy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Allergy **also known as **hypersensitivity,** is used to describe a condition in which the human body has an exaggerated response to a substance (e.g. food or drug).
 
• **Hypersensitive (also known as hypersensitivity reaction or intolerance) **refers to the immune system's unfavourable reactions, such as allergies and autoimmunity.
 
• These reactions are commonly referred to as an immune system overreaction, and they can be harmful and unpleasant.
 
• This is an immunologic phrase that should not be confused with the psychiatric term hypersensitivity, which refers to someone who is highly sensitive to physical (sound, touch, light, etc.) and/or emotional stimuli.
 
• **Pollen, moulds, animal dander, latex, certain foods, and insect stings **are examples of generally harmless substances that can cause allergies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **An infection** is the infiltration of disease-causing pathogens into an organism's bodily tissues, their multiplication, and the host tissues' reaction to the infectious agents and the toxins they create.
 
• **A mutation **is a change in an organism's DNA sequence. Mutations can occur as a result of mistakes in DNA replication during cell division, mutagen exposure, or viral infection.
 
• People use the term **"convulsion"** to describe involuntary muscle contractions.

questions.question: Where is the 'Ahom Raja’s Palace' located?

The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

__
 
• **The palace of Ahom Raja** is a historic structure in **Garhgaon, Assam, India**.
 
• The four-story palace has a dome-shaped ceiling and a chamber on the top floor.
 
• Only two of the original four watchtowers remain.
 
• On the ground floor of the palace, there are three west-facing halls.

• **Suklengmung, the 15th Ahom king, **established the **capital at Gargoan in 1540 CE **and built a palace out of wood and other ephemeral materials, according to chronicle records.

• **King Rajeswar Singha **constructed the current multi-story structure in 1752 CE.

questions.question: Who among the following scholar translated Patanjali’s work on grammar into Arabic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Al-Biruni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Al-Biruni **lived in the eastern Islamic world during an era of unprecedented political instability.
 
• He was a servant to more than six princes. Al-Biruni spent years acquiring Sanskrit and studying religious and philosophical writings in the presence of Brahmana priests and academics.
 
• Because Al-Biruni was fluent in numerous languages, he was able to compare and translate writings. He translated various Sanskrit books into Arabic, notably Patanjali's grammar work.
 
• Patanjali wrote '**Mahabhasya**; an ancient treatise on Sanskrit grammar and linguistics, based on the **Astadhyayi **of Panini. 
 
• He translated the works of Euclid (a Greek mathematician) into Sanskrit for his Brahmana companions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ibn Hajar al-Haytami** was a muhaddith and Islamic theologian from Egypt.
 
• **Ibn al-Hajj **was a Moroccan theologian and Maliki fiqh scholar. He was born in Fes and lived till 1336 in Egypt.
 
• **Ibn Hubal's **medical compendium, Kitab al-Mukhtarat fi al-Tibb, or "The Book of Selections in Medicine," was his most famous work.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with Uniform Civil Code for citizens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 44**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Uniform Civil Code** is based on the concept of one country, one code that applies to all faith groups. **Part 4 of the Indian Constitution, Article 44**, specifically mentions the term **"Uniform Civil Code."**
 
• "The State shall seek to ensure for citizens a consistent civil code across the territory of India," states Article 44.
 
• Since the first petition was filed in 2019 to seek the framing of a** UCC to promote national integration and gender justice, equality, and dignity of women,** the idea of a Uniform Civil Code in India has become a hotly disputed topic in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 45** deals with children's access to free and compulsory education. The State shall endeavour to

 provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years”.
 
• **Article 46 **promotes the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and other marginalized groups in society, as well as their protection from exploitation and social injustice.
 
• **Article 47** of The Constitution of India is one of the Directive Principles which directs the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health as among its primary duties and, in particular, the State shall endeavour to bring about prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs which are injurious to health.

questions.question: The Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015 is related to ______.

options.text: Mutual transfer of certain territories between India and Sikkim
Mutual transfer of certain territories between India and China
Mutual transfer of certain territories between India and Bangladesh
Mutual transfer of certain territories between India and Nepal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mutual transfer of certain territories between India and Bangladesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Land Boundary Agreement between India and Bangladesh **was ratified by the **Constitution (100th Amendment) Act of 2015.**
 
• In accordance with the **1974 bilateral LBA, the legislation **revised the first schedule of the constitution to exchange the disputed regions occupied by both nations.
 
• On the Indian mainland, India acquired 51 Bangladeshi enclaves (containing 7,110 acres), whereas Bangladesh received 111 Indian enclaves (covering 17,160 acres).
 
• **The India-Bangladesh Agreement **was reached in 1974, but it was never ratified because it involved territory transfer, which necessitated a constitutional amendment.
 
• The Bill modifies the Constitution's First Schedule to give effect to an agreement between India and Bangladesh on the acquisition and transfer of lands between the two countries, which was signed on May 16, 1974.
 
• The area of each state and union territory that makes up India is defined in the First Schedule of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Sino-Indian boundary dispute **is a long-running territorial dispute between China and India regarding the sovereignty of two relatively large and numerous smaller, isolated areas of land.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Mamallapuram Dance Festival organised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Every year, from early January to early February, the Mamallapuram Dance Festival **takes place for four weeks in **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• **Exponents of Bharatnatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, Mohiniattam, Odissi, and Kathak **gather in this town for this major festival to perform spellbinding performances in **Bharatnatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, Mohini Attam, Odissi, and Kathak**.
 
• Folk dancers contribute to the atmosphere and provide a touch of the local flavour that keeps everyone enthralled.
 
• The festival draws thousands of visitors from all over the world, turning this tranquil little tourist town into a hive of activity.
 
• This dance can be performed individually or in groups, and there are many powerful solo performances at Mamallapuram each year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tamil Nadu **has a long and illustrious history in the arts and entertainment. **Iyel (Literature), Isai (Music), and Nadagam (Drama)** are three types of entertainment that have their origins in rural folk theatre such as Theru Koothu (Street play).
 
• For popularity and simple entertainment value, several styles of groups and individual dances compete with classical forms.
 
• Tribal people execute a few of the dancing types. 
 
• **Mamallapuram**, also known as **Mahabalipuram**, is a town in Chengalpattu district in the southeastern Indian state of Tamil Nadu, best known for the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** of 7th- and 8th-century Hindu Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram. It is one of the famous tourist sites in India. The ancient name of the place is **Thirukadalmallai**.
 
• **Mamallapuram **was one of two major port cities in the **Pallava kingdom**. The town was named after Pallava king **Narasimhavarman I**, who was also known as **Mahabali**. Along with economic prosperity, it became the site of a group of royal monuments, many carved out of the living rock. These are dated to the 7th and 8th centuries: rathas (temples in the form of chariots), mandapas (cave sanctuaries), the giant open-air rock relief the Descent of the Ganges, and the** Shore Temple **dedicated to **Shiva**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest mountain of Bhutan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gangkhar Puensum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **With an elevation of 7,570 metres (24,836 feet) **and a prominence of 2,995 metres, **Gangkhar Puensum is Bhutan's highest mountain **and the world's highest unclimbed mountain.
 
• Its name means** "White Peak of the Three Spiritual Brothers."**
 
• It shares a border with Tibet. 
 
• A Japanese expedition ascended Liankang Kangri in 1999, a 7,535-meter (24,721-foot) subsidiary peak (not an independent summit) separated from the main peak by a 2-kilometre (1.2-mile) long ridge to the north-northwest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gipmochi** is a mountain in south-central Asia's Lower Himalayas. The peak, which rises to a height of 14,523 feet (4,427 metres), is located on the boundary between the Indian state of Sikkim and Bhutan.
 
• **Kangphu Kang,** also known as Shimokangri, is a Himalayan mountain. It is the world's 107th tallest peak, standing at 7,204 metres above sea level.
 
• **Chomolhari** is a Himalayan mountain that straddles the border between Tibet's Yadong County and Bhutan's Paro region.

questions.question: Which of the following awards did Indian politician Ghulam Nabi Azad receive in January 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Bhushan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ghulam Nabi Azad,** a veteran Congress leader and** former Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, **received the **Padma Bhushan Award in 2022**.
 
• **Ghulam Nabi Azad **is an Indian politician who served as the seventh chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir and as the Minister of Health and Family Welfare from 2005 to 2008.
 
• He was the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha until February 2021.
 
• He was India's Parliamentary Affairs Minister in former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's ministry till October 27, 2005, when he was named Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Padma Bhushan** is the Republic of India's third-highest civilian award, after the Bharat Ratna and Padma Vibhushan, and before the Padma Shri. The award, which was established on **January 2, 1954**, recognises "distinguished service of a high order...without difference of race, occupation, status, or sex."
 
• **The Padma Shri** often spelt Padma Shree, is the Republic of India's fourth-highest civilian award.
 
• **The Bharat Ratna** is the Republic of India's highest civilian honour. The award, which was established on **January 2, 1954**, is given in honour of "outstanding service/performance of the highest order," regardless of race, occupation, status, or sex.
 
• **After the Bharat Ratna, the Padma Vibhushan **is the Republic of India's second-highest civilian honour.

questions.question: ______ is used in buildings and in manufacturing processes to prevent heat loss or heat gain.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insulation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insulation **is a general term used to describe material that creates barriers to the transmission of electricity, heat, moisture, shock, or sound between insulated surfaces of adjacent bodies. These materials could be insulating heat, cold, electricity, sound, or radiation.
 
• **To reduce heat loss or gain, insulation** is utilised in buildings and manufacturing processes.
 
• Although its major goal is to save money, it also allows for more precise temperature management and worker protection.
 
• It reduces rusting caused by moisture on cold surfaces. These materials are porous and have a lot of latent air cells.
 
• The building industry uses thermal insulation to decrease heat loss or gain through the home envelope (external walls, windows, roofs, foundation, etc.).
 
• Thermal insulation provides thermal comfort inside homes by maintaining a comfortable temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The flow of a fluid (liquid or gas) between locations of differing temperatures is known as **convection**.
 
• Heat energy is transferred through collisions between surrounding atoms or molecules in** the process of conduction**. 
 
• **Solidification, commonly known as freezing**, is a phase transition in which a liquid becomes a solid when its temperature is decreased below its freezing point.

questions.question: As per the India Census figure 2011, which of the following states has the second-highest percentage contribution to the total growth of the population of India between 2001 to 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **As per the India Census figure 2011,** Bihar has the second-highest percentage contribution to the total growth of the** population of India between 2001 to 2011.**
 
• According to Census 2011 data, Bihar has a population of 104.1 million people, up from 8.30 million in 2001.
 
• According to the 2011 census, Bihar's total population is 104,099,452, with male and female populations of 54,278,157 and 49,821,295 respectively.
 
• Bihar has a sex ratio of 918 for every 1000 males, which is lower than the national average of 940, according to the census 2011. In Bihar, the female sex ratio was 919 per 1000 males in 2001.
 
• Bihar has a total size of 94,163 square kilometres. Bihar has a density of 1,106 people per square kilometre, which is greater than the national average of 382 people per square kilometre.
 
• Bihar's population density was 881 people per square kilometre in 2001, whereas the national average was 324 people per square kilometre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The 15th Indian Census, or the 2011 Census of India**, was performed in **two phases**:** house listing **and **population enumeration.**
 
• The house listing phase, which began on** April 1, 2010, **entailed gathering information about all buildings.
 
• In the first phase, data for the **National Population Register (NPR)** was collected, which would be utilised by the Unique Identification Authority of India to give a 12-digit unique identification number to all registered Indian inhabitants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bihar__:**

 
 
• **Area: 94,163 km²**
 
• **Governor: Phagu Chauhan**
 
• **Capital: Patna**
 
• **Chief minister: Nitish Kumar**

questions.question: Which of the following Nobel Laureates has written ‘Cooking to Save Your Life’ which is a book on cooking?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhijit Banerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abhijit Banerjee**, an Indian-born American economist and Nobel laureate, has written a new book (cookbook) titled** "Cooking to Save Your Life."**
 
• Juggernaut Books published the book, which was illustrated by Cheyenne Oliver, a French illustrator.
 
• In 2019, he, along with **Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer, **was awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for their innovative approach to reducing global poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Abhijit Vinayak Banerjee **is a Ford Foundation International Professor of Economics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He is an Indian-born naturalised American economist.
 
• "For their experimental approach to relieving global poverty," Banerjee shared the 2019 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amartya Sen** is an Indian economist who won the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998 for his contributions to welfare economics and social choice theory, as well as his concern for the issues that affect society's weakest members.
 
• **Maria Angelita Ressa** is a Filipino-American journalist and novelist who is also the co-founder and CEO of Rappler. She is also the **first Filipino to win the Nobel Peace Prize.**
 
• **Benjamin List** is a German chemist who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2021 for his research on asymmetric organocatalysis.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the peasant movement in Bardoli take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 **was a movement launched by** Sardar Vallabhai Patel** for the farmers of Bardoli against illegal tax increases during the independence war.
 
• **On June 12, 1928, the Bardoli Satyagraha** took place in Gujarat, India, during the British Raj, and was a major act of civil disobedience and revolt in the Indian Independence Movement.
 
• **Vallabhbhai Patel **eventually headed the movement, and its success helped pave the way for Patel to become one of the most prominent leaders of the independence struggle.
 
• Initially, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel wrote to the Governor of Bombay, demanding a reduction in taxes for the year in which the tragedies occurred. The Governor, on the other hand, ignored the letter and announced the collection as a response.
 
• The Bombay Presidency overlooked the farmers' misery and increased tax rates by 22%. 
 
• The movement was primarily concerned with the plight of wealthy and middle-class farmers, and it mostly ignored the plight of impoverished farmers. It did not bring up the issue of Hali Pratha (a kind of bonded labour system).

questions.question: In January 2022, which Indian player was named as The World Games Athlete of the Year for 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PR Sreejesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PR Sreejesh, the goalkeeper for the Indian men's hockey team, **was awarded **World Games Athlete of the Year 2021 on January 31, 2022.**
 
• He was the **first Indian male athlete to win the award** and the second Indian sportsperson overall.
 
• **Rani Rampal**, the captain of the Indian women's hockey team,** was the first Indian to receive the World Games Athlete of the Year award in 2020.**
 
• PR Sreejesh was a significant member of India's bronze-medal winning men's hockey team at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics.
 
• The 33-year-old beat off Alberto Gines Lopez, the Olympic champion in sport climbing from Spain, and Michele Giordano, an Italian wushu player, to receive the World Games Athlete of the Year 2021 honour. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rani Rampal **was named the 2019 World Games Athlete of the Year after receiving the Arjuna Award in 2016. At the 2021 Sportstar ACES Awards, Rani Rampal, the captain of the Indian women's hockey team, was named **Sportswoman of the Decade (Team Sports).**
 
• **Neeraj Chopra,** a javelin thrower, earned India's first-ever gold medal in athletics, becoming only the second Indian to do so after Abhinav Bindra, who made history in Beijing in 2008.
 
• **Pusarla Venkata Sindhu** has won medals at the Olympics and on the BWF circuit, including gold at the 2019 World Championships.

questions.question: Elephantiasis, also known as lymphatic filariasis, is caused by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**parasitic worms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Elephantiasis, or lymphatic filariasis, **is a painful and disfiguring condition. Infection with parasitic nematodes (roundworms) of the family Filariodidea is transmitted through **mosquito bites**.
 
• Mosquito-transmitted larvae land on the skin and can then enter the body. The larvae subsequently travel to lymphatic arteries, where they mature into adult worms, thus perpetuating the transmission cycle.
 
• The main symptom of elephantiasis is gross enlargement and swelling of an area of the body because of the accumulation of fluid. The arms and legs are the areas most often affected. An entire arm or leg may swell to several times its normal size resembling the thick, round appearance of an elephant's leg.
 
• **Parasitic worms, commonly known as helminths**, are huge macroparasites with adults visible to the human eye.
 
• Many of them are soil-transmitted intestinal worms that infect the gastrointestinal tract.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bacteria** are single-celled organisms with a small size. Bacteria can be found practically everywhere on the globe and are essential to its ecosystems.
 
• **Protozoa **are microscopic unicellular eukaryotes with a complex internal structure and a wide range of metabolic functions.
 
• **A virus **is a type of infectious microorganism that consists of a nucleic acid segment (DNA or RNA) encased in a protein coat.

questions.question: 'KAPILA', a programme launched on 15th October 2020 in the name of the former President of India Late Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam is associated with which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intellectual Property Literacy and Awareness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Union government** began the** Kalam Program for Intellectual Property Literacy and Awareness - KAPILA Campaign **on October 15, 2020, to promote **intellectual property literacy and patent awareness**.
 
• The then Union Minister of Education, Ramesh Pokhriyal 'Nishank,' provided details regarding the campaign in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha on February 4, 2021.
 
• According to the administration, a total of 46,556 people have signed up for KAPILA so far.
 
• On the **89th birthday of scientist and former President Late Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam**, the then Union Education Minister Ramesh Pokhriyal 'Nishank' virtually launched **KAPILA**.
 
• The government will increase awareness about the need of patenting an innovation through educational activities as part of the **KAPILA Kalam Program**, which aims to push India toward self-reliance.
 
• Its goal is to use the tools available in the field of intellectual property to help people move forward with their discoveries and turn them into patents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **From 2002 to 2007, Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam**, an Indian aerospace scientist, served as India's 11th president.
 
• He studied physics and aerospace engineering while growing up in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu.
 
• He worked as a scientist and scientific administrator for the next four decades, primarily at the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), where he was involved in India's civilian space programme and military missile development operations.

questions.question: In January 2022, who was appointed as the Chief Economic Advisor (CEA) of the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venkatraman Anantha Nageswaran**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Venkatramanan Anantha Nageswaran** is an Indian economist and the country's** 18th Chief Economic Advisor**.
 
• Between 2019 and 2021, he served as a part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council after receiving his doctorate in finance from the University of Massachusetts Amherst for his work on the empirical behaviour of exchange rates.
 
• He has also served as a visiting professor at Andhra Pradesh's Krea University, as well as a graduate student-professor at Singapore Management University and the Indian Institutes of Management Bangalore and Indore.
 
• He was appointed Chief Economic Advisor of the Government of India on January 28, 2022, succeeding **Krishnamurthy Subramanian, who served a three-year term that ended in December 2021.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Rajiv Kumar **is an Indian economist who previously served as the NITI Aayog's second vice-chairman.
 
• **Arvind Subramanian **is an Indian economist who served as the Government of India's Chief Economic Advisor from 16 October 2014 to 20 June 2018. 
 
• **Krishnamurthy Venkata Subramanian **is an Indian economist and former Chief Economic Adviser to the Government of India (CEA). He was appointed to the role on December 7, 2018, and left on October 8, 2021.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The post of** Chief Economic Adviser (CEA)** is comparable to that of Secretary to the Government of India in the Indian government.
 
• The CEA is the Indian Economic Service's ex-officio cadre controlling authority.
 
• The CEA is the head of the Economic Division of the Ministry of Finance's Department of Economic Affairs.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the animal motifs found on the cylindrical seal of the Indus region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humped bull**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The humped bull** is one of the animal motifs found on the **cylindrical seal of the Indus region**.
 
• The humped bull figurine had a molded head that was twisted to the side, and a mold was used to make the head. The body was made by hand, and the head was connected. As with the enormous hollow bull statues, the eyes were crafted with applique pupils.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Indus Cylinder Seals** are cylindrical in shape and have a completely different shape than the majority of seals found in the Indus valley; however, three cylindrical specimens have been discovered at Mohenjo-Daro, all of them in the city's upper levels, suggesting that they were also used by the inhabitants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Indus Valley Civilisation **was a Bronze Age civilization in northeastern South Asia that lasted from 3300 BCE to 1300 BCE, and from 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE in its mature form. 
 
• It was one of three early civilizations of the Near East and South Asia, together with ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia, and it was the most widespread of the three, with sites reaching from northeast Afghanistan to much of Pakistan and western and northwestern India.
